rationale:
Evidence: iteration 9 (kd 1.4) is the best design so far at 619.0. The oval finishes 20/20 at 1.80 s with max_error 0.017 and steering_oscillation 0.20, so it is not ringing. The s-bend now finishes 17/20 (progress 0.96), up from 5/20 at kd 1.2. The slalom is still 0/20, with progress 0.143 (flat since kd 1.2, 0.146). Body width is already at its maximum, so the 0.06 m off-track limit cannot move.

Single-variable kd trend at fixed geometry and gains: kd 0.8 gave s-bend progress 0.46; kd 1.0 (with sensors at y=0.06) gave 0.61; kd 1.2 gave 0.84; kd 1.4 gave 0.96. Oval steering oscillation has stayed near 0.19 to 0.20 across this range, so the extra damping adds no visible jitter. Earlier changes to kp, base_speed, wheel_track, mass and sensor span all reduced oval reliability, so I keep them fixed.

Change: kd 1.4 to 1.6, nothing else. I expect the s-bend to finish 18 to 20 of 20 with progress near 0.98 and fewer line-loss events. The slalom may gain a little, but it has plateaued, so I do not expect a large jump there. Risk: higher kd amplifies sensor noise. If oval steering_oscillation rises above about 0.3 or oval completion drops below 1.0, I will revert to kd 1.4.

Hypotheses: (H1) derivative damping still limits alternating bends, so s-bend completion keeps rising with kd. (H2) The slalom is limited by something other than damping, most likely entry speed on the sharpest alternations; a base_speed reduction only for slalom-type bends, or a different line_loss mode, is the next lever to test if kd stops helping.

Measurements next: per-track completion, progress, max_error against 0.06, line_loss_events, steering_oscillation, and oval completion_time.
